upper_boundary_stratification.definition: GT top coordinate y < 5 px versus y >= 5 px

interpretation.205: all GT-matching boxes available in the >=0.25 cache survive to the baseline output; its 38 misses are already absent at detector-cache matching stage
interpretation.215: all 16 GT-matching boxes available in the >=0.25 cache survive to the baseline output; its 74 misses are already absent at detector-cache matching stage
interpretation.217: GT-matching detector availability equals baseline output availability; the remaining issue includes localization/identity ambiguity during dense contact
interpretation.222: four GT-matching boxes present in the >=0.25 detector cache do not survive to baseline output, consistent with the separately audited duplicate-suppression loss frames
interpretation.boundary: detector recall collapses when the human GT box is truncated by the upper image boundary; this makes a boundary-focused detection experiment higher priority than adding tracker memory or ReID for IDs 205/215

next_experiment.candidate: upper-boundary padding or selective boundary ROI reinference
next_experiment.requirement: compare against the same GT with identical confidence thresholds and runtime measurements; do not promote without measured recall/precision improvement
next_experiment.why_not_global_resolution_first: previous 1280 inference improved some fused-contact boxes but was about 2.47x slower; the current evidence identifies a spatially localized boundary failure instead

limits: this cache was generated at confidence 0.25, so it cannot determine whether a missing box existed between confidence 0.10 and 0.25
detector-cache matching is a diagnostic and does not replace TrackEval
a current confidence-0.10 cache is required to separate low-confidence recovery from true detector misses for IDs 205 and 215
the boundary correlation is measured on two identities in one 90-frame interval and is not yet a general camera-edge benchmark
